newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares up for 11th straight day.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares up for 11th straight day.

text.p: Slovenian shares advanced for the 11th straight day on Tuesday, buoyed by continued demand from foreign investors.
The SBI index of seven blue chip shares rose 25.16 points, or 2.23 percent, to 1,154.90 points as foreign buyers sought shares in Slovenia's newly privatised companies.
Market participants forecast the upward momentum would continue to the end of the week but cautioned a slight downward correction may be on the horizon.
"I would predict a decline soon if only domestic investors were behind the (recent rally), but it is hard to predict the foreigners' next step," said Karmen Cerar, a trader at brokerage Poteza.

Pharmaceutical company Lek's "A" dominated turnover. Its newly privatised shares firmed 2.03 percent to 19,740 tolars, sparking interest in other recent flotations, like food companies Kolinska and Droga.
Bank Hipotekarna banka Brezice was the day's biggest gainer, firming 9.49 percent to 4,050 tolars.
The leading decliner was financial consultancy Dadas, falling 6.95 percent to 29,596 tolars.
Overall, 15 shares rose and four fell, while another five were untraded.
Total turnover fell to 433.5 million tolars ($3.1 million) from 609.9 million ($4.4 million).
